A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original estimator evaluations on synthetic, PRISM, and DICES data, including repeated-trial coverage, bias, and interval-width results in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and adds analyses of covariate-shift composition and embedding-feature correlations in Figures 6–7.

M1.justification: The persona-augmented regression, residual correction, Riesz weighting, and cross-fitting procedures remain unchanged in Equations 1–4 and Algorithms 1–3. Expanded explanations and estimand examples do not introduce a new estimation procedure.

E1.justification: The synthetic, PRISM helpfulness, and DICES safety evaluations are retained. Relabeling DICES from real-world to semi-synthetic clarifies existing coverage. The conditional estimands illustrated in Table 1 are not newly evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain Sample Average, IPW, PAR, Persona-Based, PPI++, RePPI, and DR (Classical). Figure 5 still compares DR (Riesz) with RePPI using LLM persona ratings. The added diagnostic figures introduce no comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated DICES source count from 350 to 300, consistent with the existing dataset summary. Appendix E.1 revises its surrogate-generation formula toward the clipped, range-scaled form already present in v1's main text; this does not establish a rerun. Figures 6–7 add joint content/rater-shift and embedding-dimension diagnostic sweeps.

E4.justification: New Figure 6 examines how content mixing and rater composition contribute to DICES covariate shift. New Figure 7 examines average embedding-feature correlations with ratings and domain membership across dimensions. These are limited diagnostic additions to the retained sampling-bias and persona-quality analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 40 trials per setting, 95% confidence intervals, and standard errors in Figure 4, omitting values below 0.01. The new diagnostic figures introduce no additional run-count, seed, significance-testing, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 6–7 newly report that content features dominate the measured DICES Sinkhorn distance and describe a correlation elbow near 15 embedding dimensions. Existing performance results are retained: Figure 4's DR (Riesz) average coverage remains 1.00, 0.93, and 0.86 for Synthetic, PRISM, and DICES, respectively. Existing appendix result curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Table 1 adds explicit subgroup-conditional variance and quantile estimands using the condition g(W)=1. The assumptions, theorems, and proofs in Appendices B–D remain unchanged. The removed main-text variance and quantile derivations remain available in Appendix C.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies the empirical validation by describing DICES as semi-synthetic rather than real-world and explicitly includes public PSF release among the contributions. The central claims about double robustness, general M-estimation, and estimation under sampling bias are retained.

C2.justification: Figure 6 newly interprets content shift as contributing more than rater shift to the DICES distance measure, while Figure 7 interprets the dimension-correlation trend as an elbow. Section 3 also explicitly connects 'sufficient quality' to the existing product-of-errors condition. The no-concept-drift limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 7 replaces supplementary-code and planned-release wording with a reported public code-and-data release and a repository link. Appendix E.1 revises the perturbation documentation, although its accompanying noise/bias notation remains inconsistent. Hyperparameter grids, five-fold cross-fitting, and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Byun et al. (2025), Nwankwo et al. (2025), Ulichney and Coston (2025), and Steiger et al. (2021), while removing Cai et al. (2022). Appendix A adds limited comparisons with batch-adaptive causal annotation and concurrent evaluation work addressing distribution shift and selection bias.

P1.justification: The running example changes from medical summarization to conversational safety, estimator explanations expand, and dataset terminology becomes more consistent. Main-text M-estimation exposition is replaced by a table and appendix references, and acknowledgments are added. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 and Figures 6–7, simplifies Figure 2's target-data schematic, and corrects Figure 1's source/target color description. Existing displays undergo localized resizing, relocation, and renumbering; their performance data remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and transparency through more accurate semi-synthetic framing, an estimand summary, two useful diagnostic analyses, corrected display references, and explicit code/data access information. These are bounded gains around an unchanged estimator and principal evidence. Lingering noise/bias notation inconsistencies in Appendix E.1 limit the reproducibility improvement.
